notes: Hermes' shell escape is `!cmd` in the TUI surface (`hermes chat --tui`), NOT the classic `hermes chat` REPL, which routes on `/` only. It is the direct analog of Claude Code's `!cmd`: ui-tui/src/app/useSubmission.ts:233 routes a bang-prefixed submit to gw.request('shell.exec'), and tui_gateway/server.py:18025 runs subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) and returns stdout — no LLM round-trip, no tool call. This spec adopts the same INTENT reading the claudecode sibling and the scenario description adopt (the guarded failure is 'state does not stick in working'), but on Hermes it is structural rather than a parser choice: the daemon's only signal is $HERMES_HOME/state.db, and shell.exec writes NOTHING to it — the `!cmd` echo is Ink in-memory React state (useMainApp.ts:441), verified by SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE content LIKE '!%' = 0 across the live store. So no messages row is inserted, sessions.message_count does not grow, Watcher.reconcile emits no EventActivity, and the session cannot leave ready. Two escape windows are asserted: the first before any prompt (claudecode's canonical ordering; on Hermes the sessions row does not exist yet, since it is INSERTed on the first user message per adapter.go:16-19, so that window is quiet for two reasons) and the second AFTER the turn settles, against a live store session sitting in ready — that one is the load-bearing assertion. Neither escape produces a transition, so the whole recording still carries exactly one working arc and the scenario's ready→working→ready topology and tool_calls_max:0 both hold. Anchoring follows the hermes/opencode ProcessOwnedStore shape: session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED because the ready birth comes from the processlifecycle scanner's transient proc-<PID> pre-session (the store yields no launch-time birth), and every phase from turn1_start onward pins to turn1_start via same_session_as so the pre-session cannot satisfy them. model and cost are deliberately unpinned — the recorded model depends on the config.yaml in whatever HERMES_HOME the run exports; record fills observations.model and may add cost_nonzero once the recorded model is known to be priced.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after the TUI launches. UNPINNED: the store yields no launch-time birth (the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message), so this legitimately matches the scanner's transient proc-<PID> pre-session

A PID is bound to the session. Hermes is a Python console script; the TUI launch keeps the python `hermes chat --tui` parent alive (subprocess.call, main.py:2325) so the CommandPattern matcher still resolves it

After the first `!echo hello` shell escape, state stays ready. shell.exec runs the command in the gateway process and returns stdout over RPC without writing to state.db, so the daemon's only signal never changes. Failure mode this guards: an escape mis-classified as a turn would flicker working/ready every time the user runs !ls
After the escape window, a normal user prompt drives the store-backed session ready → working — proves the session is still alive and a real prompt still drives the arc
The turn completes back to ready on the same session (assistant row with finish_reason='stop' → turn_done); state never entered waiting (no tool use)

The load-bearing assertion: a second `!echo hello-again` shell escape fired while a LIVE store session sits in ready leaves it in ready — no transition to working, none to waiting, and the session is not left stuck in working after the command exits
